intent: Bring python_pkg/wsg_grabber/tests/test_review.py under the 250-line file cap by splitting it along the same seams the source module was split on, keeping the test count identical.
scope: Non-goal: no assertion changes, no test removed or weakened
changes: Moved the rendering tests (emptiness, status_line, filename_line, title_line, render) into test_review_render.py, mirroring the source split into review._render.
Moved the undo tests into test_review_undo.py, mirroring review._undo.

Moved the two shared fixture builders _item and _reviewed into the existing conftest.py as item/reviewed, and imported them from the three test modules. Sharing them rather than copying keeps jscpd's 2% duplication gate happy.

verification.evidence: 277 passed in 15.16s -- exactly the count before the split, so no test was dropped or silently skipped by the move. Two intermediate runs failed first (4 failed, then 1 failed) because the extracted module was missing model imports and Path; those were real NameErrors surfaced by running the suite, fixed, and re-verified.
All quality hooks pass; only the evidence and contract artifact hooks remained, which this file and the paired contract satisfy.

risks: The shared builders went into conftest.py rather than a _helpers.py because the name-tests-test hook requires every other file under tests/ to match test_*.py. A _helpers.py was written first and rejected by that hook; python_pkg/syncyomi_guard/tests/conftest.py is the existing precedent for plain shared builders living in conftest.
conftest.py now mixes autouse path isolation with fixture builders. The module docstring says so explicitly.
rollback: git revert the commit; test_review.py returns to its 297-line form, the two new modules are deleted and conftest.py loses the builders.
After rollback, run python3 -m pytest python_pkg/wsg_grabber/tests/ -q and confirm it still reports 277 passed.
